featured.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
featured.tldr: In a video-plus-action world model, videos of new tasks without action labels lift out-of-distribution success on RoboTwin 2.0 from 25% to 56%, and one labeled demonstration per task lifts it to 71%.

featured.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
featured.tldr: ID-WM plans long tasks by using diffusion noise as an abstract action that picks reachable subgoals, while a second model converts each hop into precise actions.

featured.title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
featured.tldr: An agent that learns an unfamiliar game's rules, compresses them into an explicit algebraic model and formalizes it in Lean can prove levels unwinnable; it also clears all 183 public ARC-AGI-3 levels.

featured.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
featured.tldr: Rollback rewinds a learned video world model to key moments of real robot attempts, tries alternatives there, and trains on what worked, beating the average human player at ball tossing and curling within 8 hours.

featured.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts
featured.tldr: A benchmark that recombines familiar states and actions into new goals shows world models fail even when every ingredient was seen in training, and contact-rich tasks fail even with true state as input.

featured.title: Agentic World Action Models
featured.tldr: AW-0 adds a code-writing expert to a robot world action model, jointly generating a skill program, future video and actions, and beats vision-language-action and world-model baselines on RoboTwin 2.0 and real tasks.

featured.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
featured.tldr: WildAWM uses open models to synthesize 341 verifiable, long-horizon computer-use tasks across GUI, command line and MCP, and RL on them improves Qwen models on all eight unseen benchmarks.

featured.title: Rethinking World-Action Model for Compositional and In-Context Robotic Manipulation
featured.tldr: ViGAR splits robot manipulation into a planner that imagines the next subgoal as an image and a world-action model that executes it, reaching 82.00% and 67.02% on RoboTwin Clean2Random, 12.86 points above the best baseline.

featured.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
featured.tldr: Long-WAM shows that robot policies only benefit from long visual history when their video backbone was pretrained autoregressively, and makes this fast enough for real-time control on edge GPUs.

featured.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
featured.tldr: RoboJEPA scales a latent robot world model from 22 million to 8 billion parameters and finds a predictable compute scaling law whose offline error tracks robot planning success.

featured.title: PointWAM: 3D World Action Modeling for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
featured.tldr: PointWAM forecasts how a scene and the robot's hands move as 3D point trajectories, letting it pre-train on 1.15 million human videos and then beat strong vision-language-action models on dexterous manipulation.

featured.title: Native Action-Prior Learning from Videos for World Action Models
featured.tldr: NAVA-WAM pretrains a robot's action module directly on action-free videos by making video prediction depend on it, beating prior methods on LIBERO and RoboTwin and succeeding on 14 of 15 real-robot trials.
